entry.title: Research Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: This section is anchored by the Hermes Agent v0.21.4 release (21 September 2026), which adds a --format stream-json CLI flag for structured output alongside a rollup of merged PRs covering skills auto-load and MCP discovery concurrency — the freshest, most directly actionable news for Hermes users. Two companion deep-dives cover the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: its end-to-end request pipeline with process isolation driving the unmodified official Claude CLI, and its credential model where auth lives entirely inside the official Claude Code CLI (no API keys handled by Hermes) — essential trust-and-setup reading for the plugin's growing user base. Rounding out the ecosystem: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 (18 September 2026) hardens MCP security with per-invocation session scoping and adds vector-store connectors, relevant for teams building across agent SDKs; and AgentProto, a new open-source TypeScript runtime that integrates Hermes as one of 14 supported coding agents, signaling Hermes's expanding interoperability in the broader agent orchestration landscape.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Documents Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21), released 21 September 2026, which adds a --format stream-json flag to the CLI. The flag emits structured JSONL — one JSON object per line — instead of plain text, enabling reliable parsing by scripts and pipelines. Upgrade paths include hermes update for git installs, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The same release reportedly rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency, at no extra cost since it is built into the open-source agent.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Explains the end-to-end architecture of the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: Hermes talks to the plugin, which drives the unmodified official Claude Code executable, with conversation flowing as native stream-json while Hermes retains its own loop, tools and approvals. Key mechanics: every request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools/skills disabled so Hermes' tool inventory is what the model sees; an admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request per turn and rejects native retry attempts locally to keep billing honest. Version requirements are Hermes 0.21.4+ and Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 (qualified version), logged in. No forked CLI or patched binary is involved.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Details the authentication design of the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin. Auth lives entirely in the official Claude Code CLI: the user runs claude auth login once (browser plus pasted code), and the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes or prints credential files. No API key exists anywhere in the flow; the plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint and cloud overrides, naming conflicting variables without exposing their values. Status checks are local via claude auth status, reading the credential store in roughly 0.3s, and separated setups are supported through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR pointing at a dedicated CLI-managed config.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Coverage of Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, tagged on GitHub on 18 September 2026. Headline changes center on MCP security: sessions scoped per invocation with requests authenticated against the correct invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives become ZIP-only with digest verification, ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected, and new vector-store connectors were added for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB and Azure Cosmos DB plus in-memory and portable filters. The post flags breaking changes, notably deprecation of the MCP sampling callback, and warns readers to review before upgrading.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: A review of AgentProto, a new open-source agentic runtime written in TypeScript that provides a single interface to start, message, watch and stop coding agents, with quality gates before work lands. Its 22 September 2026 release (v0.20.0) integrates 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode and Mastra. The project is Apache-2.0 licensed and free apart from underlying model usage. The reviewer notes it is very early — single-digit GitHub stars, Tier 2 components labeled alpha scaffolding — and concludes it is interesting architecturally but early-adopters-only for now.
